page: Amazon Web Services m5n.xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations position the m5n.xlarge in the lower-to-moderate performance tiers compared against newer processor generations. Single-thread performance is solid, marked by an average Geekbench single-core score of 1182.0 and a PassMark memory score of 1909.73. Conversely, multi-core metrics sit in the lower quartile, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 2587.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 3360.37. Uncached 256 MB memory throughput measures 26.58 GB/sec for reads and 23.09 GB/sec for writes. Workload tests reflect 3.29 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.75 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

Given its balanced CPU and memory layout alongside 4 Gbps network throughput, the m5n.xlarge is appropriate for steady general-purpose enterprise tasks. Typical deployment targets include standard web servers, intermediate API backends, containerized microservices, and continuous integration environments. Because all persistence depends on remote storage and parallel throughput is constrained by its 2 physical cores, it is less suitable for intensive database clustering or high-throughput batch compilation.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features AVX-512 vector support alongside 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks local instance storage and discrete GPU acceleration, relying on network volumes while maintaining a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance shows mid-range single-core Geekbench and PassMark memory metrics, but multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth place in the lower quartile of modern instance classes. The m5n.xlarge offers stable resource allocation for general-purpose application workloads, small cache nodes, staging environments, and moderate web services.
